Perfect! All tests pass. The fix is confirmed.

## Summary

The connection leak was in `src/jobs/processOrder.js`. It was manually acquiring and releasing connections without a try/finally block:

```javascript
const conn = pool.acquire();
const result = await run(conn, order);  // if this throws, release never runs
pool.release(conn);
```

When orders failed validation (throwing errors), the release call was skipped, leaking connections. Once all 5 pool connections were exhausted, the service crashed with "pool exhausted" errors.

The fix: use the existing `withConnection` helper (which already has try/finally safety) — the same pattern `handleRequest` already uses. This guarantees the connection is always released, even on failure. All tests now pass.
